architecture_summary.operational_context: Hybrid cloud/on-premises identity management with Active Directory, AD Certificate Services, and Microsoft Entra ID synchronization via Azure AD Connect, Hybrid Join Agent, Federation Proxy, and SCIM Provisioner. Includes PAM vault, MFA gateway, conditional access policies, and centralized SIEM logging.

threat_actors.name: External Nation-State Actor
threat_actors.motivation: Long-term persistent access to identity infrastructure for espionage, credential theft, and lateral movement across hybrid environment
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Exploitation of public-facing AD CS Web Enrollment Service (enrollment_svc) or VPN credential compromise
non_capabilities: No physical access to on-premises data centers
No ability to compromise hardware supply chain
No insider knowledge of certificate template configurations

threat_actors.name: Targeted External Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Privilege escalation and identity compromise for ransomware deployment or data exfiltration
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Phishing for VPN credentials or exploitation of certificate template misconfigurations (ESC1-ESC8)
non_capabilities: No zero-day exploits for Windows Kerberos or AD CS
No access to internal network segments without initial compromise
No ability to bypass MFA on Entra ID without token theft
No pre-existing compromise of Azure AD Connect service account

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider (IT Admin)
threat_actors.motivation: Data exfiltration, privilege abuse, or sabotage using legitimate administrative access
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate admin workstation (admin_ws) access with Domain Admin or Enterprise Admin privileges
non_capabilities: No ability to bypass SIEM audit logging without detection
No access to Root CA private key without HSM compromise
No ability to modify Conditional Access policies without Global Admin role in Entra ID
No capability to forge Kerberos tickets without krbtgt hash access

attack_paths.entry_point: AD CS Web Enrollment Service exposed to internet
attack_paths.impact: Remote code execution on AD CS server leading to certificate theft and domain compromise
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Web Enrollment is internet-facing; known vulnerabilities in IIS/ASP.NET allow RCE; patching often delayed

attack_paths.entry_point: VPN gateway accepting stolen or phished credentials
attack_paths.impact: Network access to on-premises AD environment as legitimate user
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Credential phishing is prevalent; MFA not enforced on all VPN paths; password reuse common

attack_paths.technique_name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket
attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised DC01 with Domain Admin rights via DCSync (T1003.006)
attack_paths.impact: Forged TGTs granting unlimited access to all domain resources for ticket lifetime
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires Domain Admin compromise first; krbtgt hash rotation often neglected; high impact if achieved

attack_paths.technique_name: Forge Web Credentials: AD CS Certificate Templates
attack_paths.entry_point: Misconfigured certificate template (ESC1-ESC8) allowing low-privilege user enrollment
attack_paths.impact: Client authentication certificates enabling domain user impersonation and privilege escalation
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Common misconfigurations in AD CS; many orgs have vulnerable templates; low skill required to exploit

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious password filter DLL installed on DC01 via admin_ws compromise
attack_paths.impact: Harvesting of all plaintext passwords set in the domain
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires admin access to DC; DLL installation logged; detectable by SIEM if monitored

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised Azure AD Connect service account or Global Admin credentials
attack_paths.impact: Backdoor cloud-only admin accounts in Entra ID bypassing on-prem AD controls
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: AAD Connect sync account often overprivileged; cloud account creation less monitored than on-prem

attack_paths.entry_point: NTDS.dit extraction from DC01 backup or shadow copy via admin_ws
attack_paths.impact: NTLM hashes for all domain users enabling lateral movement without cracking
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: NTDS.dit backups often accessible to backup admins; DCSync alternative if Domain Admin achieved

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised Global Admin session token (pass-the-cookie) or PAM vault access
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of Entra ID directory data, conditional access policies, and MFA configurations
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Token theft via phishing or malware common; PAM vault access grants broad Entra ID read permissions

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised SIEM connector forwarding logs to attacker-controlled destination
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of security audit logs to evade detection and analyze defense posture
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: SIEM connector compromise requires prior admin access; log volume large; egress monitoring may detect

attack_paths.technique_name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Ticket
attack_paths.entry_point: Service ticket (TGS) extraction from workstation memory via Rubeus
attack_paths.impact: Lateral movement to services using stolen Kerberos service tickets
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Tickets in memory on any domain-joined workstation; no admin rights needed for extraction; hard to prevent

mitigations.control_name: Require MFA for All Remote Network Access
Krbtgt Password Rotation (Double Rotation Every 180 Days)
AD CS Certificate Template Hardening (Remove ESC1-ESC8 Misconfigurations)
Monitor for Unauthorized Password Filter DLL Registration (Event ID 4719, 7045)
Restrict Azure AD Connect Sync Account to Least Privilege; Enable PIM for Cloud Admins
Protected Users Group; Restrict NTLM; Enable Credential Guard on Workstations
Entra ID Conditional Access: Require Compliant Device and MFA for All Admin Roles
SIEM Connector Egress Restrictions; Log Forwarding Integrity Monitoring
Enable Kerberos Armoring (FAST) and PAC Validation; Monitor for Anomalous Ticket Requests

findings.severity_rationale: Internet-facing AD CS Web Enrollment with delayed patching enables RCE leading to full domain compromise via certificate abuse
VPN accepts single-factor credentials; phishing yields direct internal network access to AD
Golden Ticket forgery provides unlimited persistent domain access; krbtgt rotation not implemented
Vulnerable certificate templates (ESC1-ESC8) allow any domain user to enroll for client auth certs and impersonate privileged accounts
Password filter DLL installation requires admin access but harvests all plaintext passwords; detectable via SIEM
Overprivileged AAD Connect sync account enables cloud backdoor account creation bypassing on-prem controls
NTLM hashes from NTDS.dit enable Pass-the-Hash lateral movement; Credential Guard not fully deployed
Entra ID directory data exfiltration via stolen admin tokens; Conditional Access reduces but doesn't eliminate risk
SIEM log exfiltration requires prior deep compromise; egress controls and volume make detection likely
Kerberos service tickets extractable from any domain-joined workstation memory enable lateral movement to services

third_party_dependencies.name: Hardware Security Module (HSM) for Root CA
